newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday May 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday May 7.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The government confortably won a confidence vote in the chamber of deputies (lower house) called to speed approval of a controversial mini-budget said to be vital to Italy's drive to join Europe's single currency (all).

* Prime minister Romano Prodi said that changes to Italy's pensions system would not be implemented until January 1, 1998, as outlined under a landmark 1995 pension deal. In a TV programme, Prodi added he favoured a "redistribution" rather than a reduction of welfare spending and that early retirement should not be encouraged (all).

* A report by national statistics institute ISTAT showed Italy's consumer price index rose 1.7 percent year-on-year in April against 2.2 percent in March, the tamest rate of growth since April 1969 (all).

* In an interview about the privatisation of electricity group Eni and Enel, industry minister Pierluigi Bersani said the government had done its duty and it was time private investors provided fresh capital to the sector (Corriere della Sera).

* Retailing group Rinascente said it was launching a 780 billion lire capital increase in shares, bonds and warrants. A statement by the group said it was to buy Italian interests of French retail retail group Auchan for 530 billion lire (all).

* State-controlled telecoms holding Stet's managing director Tomaso Tommasi di Vignano confirmed the group was in talks with multi-media group Mediaset to set up an Italian digital platform for satellite television services. Tommasi di Vignano added the group was seeking an international ally and would choose a partner by the end of the year (all).
* Insurer INA said 1996 parent net profit rose 6.4 percent to 421 billion lire and it proposed paying a dividend of 65 lire against the previous year's 55 lire (Sole 24 Ore).

* Silvio Scaglia, managing director of Italy's second mobile phone operator Omnitel, said the group should break even in 1997 at the operating level, before interest payments and taxes. The largest shareholder in Omnitel is Olivetti with a stake of 35.5 percent (La Repubblica).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
